A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study despite the revised title and benchmark name. All 20 pages, including tables, figures, equations and Appendices A–E, are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six multimodal models, prompting interventions and qualitative analyses in Tables 2–7 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the model comparisons, clarification experiments and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The data-generation procedure and persona, chain-of-thought and clarification procedures are unchanged. The punctuation edit in the persona prompt does not change its instructions.

E1.justification: RUMS renames iReason without changing coverage. Both retain object absence, referential ambiguity, factual contradiction and goal feasibility, using the same ActiveVision, GQA, MMIR and synthesized images.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same six models: o3, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LLaVA-NeXT-7B, InternVL2.5-8B and Phi-3.5-Vision-4B. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Model versions and sizes, sample counts, explicit yes/no evaluation, LLM-judge scoring and clarification protocols remain unchanged in Sections 2–4 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the same implicit-versus-explicit comparison, reasoning-versus-answer analysis, prompting interventions and Appendix D case studies. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both report point accuracies without seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 2–7 and qualitative outcomes in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. For example, Table 6 retains forced-clarification accuracies of 94.62% for o3 and 96.32% for GPT-4o.

T1.justification: The task definitions and scoring formulas in Table 6 and Appendix D.2.2 are unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction findings and conclusion retain the same claims about implicit-reasoning failures, latent competence and prompting interventions. The new title and benchmark name do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning compliance, alignment and suppressed reasoning are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning templated prompts, static image–text pairs and generalization across models.

D1.justification: Appendices A–E retain identical curation instructions, evaluation prompts, implementation references and planned data-release terms. The persona-prompt punctuation edit adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 5, the references and comparisons with earlier benchmarks are unchanged. Renaming the diagnostic suite does not revise its novelty claims or research positioning.

P1.justification: The subtitle changes from 'Probing Implicit Reasoning in Multimodal Language Models' to 'Reasoning in Underspecified and Misspecified Scenarios for Multimodal LLMs.' iReason becomes RUMS, and one persona-prompt dash becomes a comma. Section organization is unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer title alters the title-block layout, renamed passages undergo local reflow, and Table 1's caption changes to 'RUMS Statistics.' Figures, table structures and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 changes the title, benchmark name and minor presentation details while retaining the same scientific content and Appendices A–E. These edits do not materially improve or impair the paper's evidence, reproducibility or readability.
